entries.not_relevant_because: The manuscript 'A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent' proves that the border determinantal complexity of the m×m complex permanent is at least c·m³ for m ≥ 1408 (c = 1/(5529600e)), and the same cubic bound for exact determinantal complexity and for vertex and edge counts of affine-linear algebraic branching programs. Everything is in the algebraic model over ℂ with affine-linear determinant representations. The text never mentions Turing machines, polynomial-time decision procedures, certificates, or the classes P and NP. Its only link to the problem is Valiant's algebraic framework (VP versus VNP), where a superpolynomial determinantal complexity of the permanent would separate the algebraic classes. A polynomial bound does not do that, and the manuscript itself says that whether the permanent has superpolynomial determinantal or border determinantal complexity 'remains open'.
